subject: history
topicName: Youth and Education in Nazi Germany

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The Hitler Youth was made compulsory by law on 1 December 1936. By 1939, over 8.7 million young people (over 90% of eligible youth) were members. The organisation aimed to indoctrinate young Germans with Nazi ideology and prepare boys for military service.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The Bund Deutscher Mädel (BDM) was the girls' equivalent of the Hitler Youth. By 1939, it had over 2 million members. The BDM focused on physical fitness, domestic skills, and motherhood training - preparing girls to be healthy mothers for the Aryan race.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The BDM emphasised that a woman's highest duty was to bear healthy Aryan children. Members were taught that education was less important than physical fitness and motherhood. The BDM motto was: "Be faithful, be pure, be German." Members who became pregnant out of wedlock were not punished - the Nazis valued Aryan births regardless of marital status.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The Nazis took complete control of the education system. All teachers had to join the Nazi Teachers' League (NSLB) - by 1936, 97% had joined. The curriculum was rewritten to reflect Nazi ideology, and textbooks were replaced with racially "correct" versions.

steps.body: Explain two ways the Nazis controlled education. (4 marks) | How far did the Hitler Youth succeed in indoctrinating young Germans? (8 marks) | "Youth resistance in Nazi Germany was ineffective." How far do you agree? (12 marks)
